griffin_get_current_date.description: Read device clock. Response is exactly 10 bytes: [0x74, status, reserved (4B), unix_time u32le].

griffin_get_dataset_info.description: Dataset (history buffer) info. Request carries a dataset offset byte. Response after the 2-byte header: base_time u32le (unix seconds; all-0xFF = none), dataset_number u8, slot_count u8, session_id u16le, then TWO u16le both equal to the record count (23,23 later 24,24 in the long capture; possibly record_count plus last-record sequence). Long-capture behavior: slot_count is the number of completed 5-minute slots in the pending hour — it read 3, then 8 after ~26 more minutes, then 11, tracking wall clock at one per 300 s and wrapping each hour as record_count increments (records are hourly rollups). base_time stayed fixed at the device's boot/reset time. NOTE: opcode 0x02 collides with the legacy "delete measurements" opcode — on Griffin firmware 0x02 means dataset info.

griffin_read_external_flash_image_versio.description: Read external flash firmware image version. Response is 6 bytes: [0x72, status, major, minor, patch, build]; version string is "major.minor.patch" (0xFF = invalid). Requires G-BLE >= 1.2.1. Capture: firmware reported external image 2.3.1 alongside BLE firmware G-BLE-2.2.3.

griffin_region.description: RF region commands (not exercised in the capture): 0x76 = set region null, 0x77 = set EU, 0x78 = set North America, 0x79 = get region.

griffin_report_measurements.description: Fetch the pending-hour history block (capture-verified on G-BLE-2.2.3). Same 9-byte shape as the legacy report-measurements command, but sent as ATT Write Command (write without response) and, on Griffin firmware, byte 1 selects the DATASET rather than a legacy operator: the vendor app sent 0x02 immediately after dataset info reported dataset_number 2. All remaining bytes zero. The device answers with a single 230-byte notification on the ASR characteristic (b42e538a — format documented there; needs ATT MTU >= 233), followed by an ASRACP indication [0x01, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00] (opcode echo, status, likely-block-count u16le, trailing u16 zero). Enable ASR notifications and ASRACP indications first.

dataset_number.description: Dataset to read; use dataset_number from griffin_get_dataset_info (0x02 in capture).

griffin_self_check.description: Self check / device info. Response (30 bytes max): [0x6D, status, uptime_u32le, device_type, reserved, msp_version (2B), ...]. device_type: 0=unknown, 1=Wave 2, 2=Wave Plus, 3=Wave Mini. Capture: response byte 6 was 0x01 (WAVE2), uptime ~14 h. Long-capture observations on the undocumented tail (all MEDIUM): bytes 24-25 u16le incremented across app sessions (45, 46, 47, 49 — a connection counter?); bytes 26-27 u16le held 0x0A4F = 2639, the same value the ASR history block carries where 0.01-scaled radon (26.39 Bq/m³) fits; bytes 28-29 u16le held 0x0009, equal to the advertisement flags word.

griffin_set_current_date.description: Set device clock to unix time (seconds, little-endian).

griffin_ui_settings.description: Read/write UI settings. Sub-command byte: 0=GET, 1=SET, 2=SET_TO_DEFAULT. GET response after the 2-byte header: humidity upper-yellow u8, upper-red u8, lower-yellow u8, lower-red u8 (%RH), radon yellow/red u16le (Bq/m³), VOC yellow/red u16le (ppb), CO₂ yellow/red u16le (ppm), then a settings byte (lower nibble = light setting, upper nibble = sound setting) and an indicator byte (lower nibble = alive-indicator, upper nibble bit 0 = alarm, bit 1 = B2C). Capture GET returned defaults: radon 100/150, VOC 250/2000, CO₂ 800/1000, humidity 25/30/60/70.

report_measurements.description: Request stored measurement records from a sensor dataset.

format_A.description: Indicate which optional fields to include
format_A.name: flags

manufacturer_data.description: Serial number and status flags in manufacturer data.
Airthings BTSIG manufacturer ID 0x0334. Manufacturer data contains 4-byte serial number at offset 0 and 2-byte flags at offset 4.

format.description: Device serial number (little-endian — all three official Airthings readers decode LE, e.g. wave-reader struct '<HLH')
format.name: serial_number

format.description: Bitfield: bit 0 = error, bit 1 = RTC not set, bit 2 = wait, bit 3 = wave disabled, bit 5 = ring spinning blue, bit 6 = waved in last 5 min, bit 7 = pairing mode, bit 8 = new 5-min data, bit 9 = new 60-min data, bits 10-11 = ring color (0=auto, 1=white, 2=green, 3=yellow, 4=red), bit 12 = hub connected (GriffinScanResultData), bit 15 = POST failed. Capture-validated: a Wave Gen 2 advertised flags 0x0021 (bits 0+5, error + ring spinning blue, seen during device setup). Long-capture (44 min steady state, same unit): flags held 0x0009 with bit 0x0002 additionally raised for ~20 s once every 300 s — a beacon that a fresh 5-minute sample was just taken (the pulses align with the device's 5-minute sampling tick; clients can scan for this bit as a wake-on-new-data signal instead of polling). The 0x0009 value is echoed as the last u16 of the Griffin self-check response, corroborating the little-endian decode — but note the pulsing bit then lands on "RTC not set" and the steady bits on "error"/"wave disabled" in the app's table above, so the app bit NAMES fit the observed behavior poorly on Griffin firmware; treat the pulse timing as capture-fact and the bit labels as MEDIUM confidence.
format.name: flags

device.name: Airthings Wave Family
device.notes:
Family of BLE air quality monitors: Wave (radon), Wave Plus (radon + CO₂ + VOC + pressure), Wave Mini (temp/humidity/mold risk), Wave Gen 2, View Plus (particulate + display), and Hub (gateway). All devices share a common GATT profile architecture (AtGattProfile) with per-model service UUIDs, manufacturer ID 820 (0x0334) in advertisement data, and a standardized ASR/ASRACP protocol for reading sensor data and controlling the device.
DISCOVERY: Scan for service UUIDs in advertisement. Manufacturer data (company ID 820) carries 4-byte serial number followed by 2-byte flags. Device type identified by which service UUID is present in the advertisement itself (ADV_IND incomplete 128-bit service UUID list) — the HCI capture shows the scan response is empty on Wave Gen 2.
COMMUNICATION: Connect to the air sensor service UUID. Sensor data read via two paths: 1. Standard BLE GATT characteristics (temperature 2A6E, humidity 2A6F,
   pressure 2A6D, dew point 2A7B) — read directly or via notify.
2. ASR (Air Sensor Read) characteristic — notifications carry packed
   multi-sensor data records. ASRACP (Access Control Point) used to
   request historical data dumps, configure device settings, set time, etc.
   On newer firmware the ASRACP characteristic multiplexes two command
   sets: the legacy ASRACP opcodes (0x01-0x04, 0xF8/0xF9) and the newer
   "Griffin" direct opcodes (0x02 dataset info, 0x66 UI settings, 0x6D
   self check, 0x72-0x74 clock/flash, 0x76-0x79 region), the latter
   confirmed by HCI capture on Wave Gen 2 firmware G-BLE-2.2.3.

CONFIDENCE: Service/characteristic UUIDs are HIGH — sourced directly from the app's own per-model UUID tables; Wave Gen 2 ASR/ASRACP/combined UUIDs additionally exercised in capture. Advertisement serial/flags layout is HIGH — capture-verified (serial 2950016244 matches the LE decode; flag bits match the app's WaveScanResultData and legacy DeviceDefines bit tables). Combined sensor-data packet format is HIGH on Wave Gen 2 — 20-byte record captured and decoded against the app's CurrentValuesParser. ASRACP opcode protocol is HIGH — full opcode/format tables extracted and the Griffin subset observed live. Note opcode 0x02 is overloaded: legacy "delete measurements" vs Griffin "dataset info"; the captured firmware answered 0x02 with dataset info. ASR notification framing on Griffin firmware is HIGH for Wave Gen 2 — the long capture contains a full history readout: a report-measurements write on ASRACP answered by ONE 230-byte ASR notification carrying the pending hour as twelve 5-minute slots (format on the Wave 2 ASR characteristic below), cross-validated slot-by-slot against the combined-characteristic reads in the same session. The legacy multi-record ASR framing described in the app (flags byte + optional fields per record) was NOT what the Griffin firmware sent and remains MEDIUM, app-derived only. Security is MEDIUM — ATCommandSetFrame suggests optional PIN/challenge auth but flow not fully decoded; the captured session ran entirely without pairing, bonding, or encryption (no SMP traffic).

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The device does expose a pairing-mode state — bit 7 of the sensor flags field reports it — but nothing in the documented surface needs it. Reading the flag is useful for showing a user what the device thinks it is doing; entering the mode is not a prerequisite for anything here.

pairing.notes: A 44-minute HCI capture of four vendor-app sessions, including a full history readout, contains zero SMP traffic: sensor reads, DIS reads and every ASRACP write ran unauthenticated over an unencrypted link. So nothing is required. A central may still bond on its own initiative and the device will accept it, which is why `bonding` is optional rather than none — and why the rejoin note tells a user to clear the OS bond if one exists. An optional PIN/challenge path may exist for operations the capture did not exercise; the app's command-set frame parsing hints at one, but it was never seen on the wire.

credentials.notes: BLE-only for sensor access. Hub variant adds WiFi but config is done via BLE.

factory_reset.description:
Worth stating loudly because the obvious search leads somewhere wrong. Airthings DOES document a reset button, at length, with a five-second hold that clears WiFi and Bluetooth pairing and shows a countdown on the display — and all of that belongs to the VIEW series, a different product. A Wave Plus, Wave Radon or Wave Mini has neither the button nor the display, so someone following those instructions is looking for a control that does not exist on the device in their hand.
There is also little for a reset to clear: the Wave is BLE-only, holds no network credentials, and never bonds (an HCI capture of a full vendor-app session shows no SMP traffic at all — see `pairing`). A new client just connects. Removing the batteries restarts the sensor, but no vendor source describes that as clearing anything.
factory_reset.effect: Nothing to reset. The Wave family has no reset control and no documented factory-reset procedure: the vendor manual describes activation as pulling the battery tab and pairing as an in-app step, and no button is described anywhere on the housing.

methods.description: Scan for Airthings service UUIDs (manufacturer ID 820), connect, read standard BLE characteristics for live readings, or use ASR/ASRACP for historical data and configuration.

steps.action: Scan for Airthings devices via manufacturer ID 820 in advertisement data.
Identify device type by service UUID in scan response.
Connect and read sensor data via standard BLE characteristics or ASR notifications.

setup.notes: No provisioning required. BLE connection only. Device scan filters per-model service UUID. No pairing or PIN required for sensor reads or for the ASRACP writes observed in the HCI capture (no SMP traffic). An optional password/PIN path may still exist for other operations (ATCommandSetFrame parsing suggests a challenge-response auth path, not exercised in the capture).

rejoin.notes: Unpair from OS Bluetooth settings if bonded, then reconnect.

testing.notes:
Nobody on this project has driven an Airthings unit from this document. What exists is two local Nordic-sniffer HCI captures of the VENDOR app talking to a Wave Gen 2 on firmware G-BLE-2.2.3 -- the second 44 minutes of steady state across four app sessions -- held in the research store and not committed. Those captures are what "capture-verified" means everywhere it appears below: the advertisement layout, the combined packet, the ASRACP Griffin command set, the 230-byte pending-hour history block and the "new 5-minute data" flag pulse were each read off real traffic.
That is stronger than static analysis and weaker than driving the device, and the gap matters here: a capture shows the vendor app's happy path only. The other five models in the family were never on the wire, the ASR history RECORD format was not exercised inside the capture window, and no write this spec documents has been sent by anything but the vendor's own app.

variants.notes: Radon-only monitor. Sensors: radon 24h avg, radon long-term avg, temperature, humidity. Device type code: dTWave=1 in legacy code. Sensor indices: 0=radon24h, 2=longTerm, 3=temp, 4=humidity, 5=status.

Updated Wave with Gen 2 hardware. Different service UUID and ASR/ASRACP characteristic UUIDs. Same sensor suite as Gen 1. ASR: b42e538a, ASRACP: b42e50d8, Combined: b42e4dcc. Serial number prefix 2950 (InstrumentTypePrefix.WAVE_2); BLE firmware is named "G-BLE-x.y.z" (capture: G-BLE-2.2.3-master+0). Capture-verified (airthings_2950_wave_capture.pcapng): b42e4a8e is advertised in ADV_IND, the combined characteristic returns the 20-byte packet documented below, and the ASRACP characteristic accepts the Griffin command set (self check, dataset info, clock, UI settings, external flash version) over write/indicate with no pairing. Self-check response byte 6 = device type 0x01 (WAVE2). The long capture additionally verified the history readout: ASRACP report-measurements → single 230-byte pending-hour block on the ASR characteristic (twelve 5-minute slots; format on b42e538a), and the advertisement's ~20 s "new 5-minute data" flag pulse every 300 s.

Radon + CO₂ + VOC + temperature + humidity + pressure. Device type code: dTWavePlus=2 in legacy code. ASR: b42e2fc2, ASRACP: b42e2d06, Combined: b42e2a68. Includes dew point characteristic (2A7B) and pressure (2A6D).

Compact temp/humidity/mold risk monitor. No radon. Smallest form factor. Same common GATT profile with ASR/ASRACP. The BLE packet on the combined data characteristic (b42e3b98, struct "<2B5HLL") also carries pressure and VOC, beyond the temp/humidity the marketing description suggests.
Humidifier variant. Referenced in Instrument.Type enum (WAVE_MIST_GEN_1) but no separate GATT profile found in this APK version. May share service UUID with Mini.
Air quality monitor with display. Particulate matter (PM) + radon + CO₂. Uses Albatross GATT profile with product provisioning service b42eb4a6 for WiFi/BLE configuration. Alias: "Albatross" in code.
Gateway/hub device. Bridges sub-devices to cloud. Limited sensor data available directly via BLE.

entities.name: Radon 24h Average
entities.notes: Previously also claimed for Wave Plus, but this characteristic lives on the Gen 1 air sensor service (b42e1f6e) and was never confirmed on Plus hardware — the vendor app reads Plus radon from the combined packet, which the Wave Plus entity below now binds.

entities.name: Radon 1h Average
entities.notes: The Gen 1 service's third dedicated radon characteristic, previously documented but bound to no entity. The hourly figure reacts a day before the 24 h average does; Airthings' own banding (100/150 Bq/m³) is defined on averages, so treat a brief spike here as a prompt to watch the averages, not a verdict by itself.

entities.name: Radon 24h Average
entities.notes: Capture-verified field of the Wave Gen 2 combined packet.

entities.name: Temperature
entities.notes: Combined-packet field, capture-verified (22.57-22.66 °C tracking the vendor app's own reading). Ordered before the SIG characteristic — see the comment above the entities block.

entities.name: Temperature
entities.notes: The Mini's combined packet is centikelvin; the format block's scale 0.01 + value_offset -273.15 already produce °C, and this entity restates only the display unit. The vendor's wavemini-reader decodes current values exclusively from this packet.

entities.name: Temperature
entities.notes: SIG-characteristic binding, scoped to the models with no decodable combined packet: Gen 1 (the vendor's wave-reader reads exactly this; its combined characteristic has no recovered format) and View Plus (no model-specific characteristics recovered at all). Unscoped, this entity applied to every variant and doubled the reading beside the combined-packet bindings above. App-derived; unobserved in capture.

entities.name: Humidity
entities.notes: Combined-packet field, capture-verified (107 raw = 53.5 %RH at the packet's 0.5 %RH per count). Ordered before the SIG characteristic — see the comment above the entities block.

entities.name: Humidity
entities.notes: SIG-characteristic binding, scoped to the models with no decodable combined packet — same reasoning as the temperature entity above.

entities.name: Pressure
entities.notes: The Mini is not documented to expose the standard pressure characteristic (2A6D); its combined packet is the only known source.

entities.name: Ambient Light
entities.notes: On the Mini the light byte sits at offset 0 of the combined packet, not offset 2 — see the format block's note on the two vendor decoders.

helpful_urls.description: Vendor manual for the Wave Plus. Confirms the family has no reset control and that pairing is an in-app step.
helpful_urls.title: Airthings Wave Plus user manual (PDF)

security.notes: Standard BLE GATT connection — no mandatory bonding or pairing for reading sensor data. HCI capture of a full vendor-app session (airthings_2950_wave_capture.pcapng) shows no SMP traffic at all: combined-data reads, DIS reads, and every ASRACP write (Griffin command set, including clock set and UI settings) ran unauthenticated over an unencrypted link. The 44-minute long capture (four app sessions, including the full history readout) likewise contains zero SMP traffic. Whether the legacy ATCommandSetFrame challenge-response path (AT+CHALLENGE, AT+CMD) gates any additional operations remains unconfirmed — it was not exercised in the capture.

timing.notes: Capture-observed cadence (Wave Gen 2, G-BLE-2.2.3): environment sensors (temperature/humidity/ambient light) sample every 300 seconds; twelve 5-minute slots roll up into one stored hourly record (dataset record_count advanced once per hour, slot counter 0-11 in dataset info). For ~20 seconds after each 5-minute sample the advertisement raises a flags bit (see identification.manufacturer_data), so a passive scanner can wake on new data instead of polling. Radon is exposed as 24 h / long-term averages and updates on the hourly tick. Sensor read via BLE is real-time upon connection + notification enable.

format.name: flags
format.notes: Bit 0=baseTimePresent, bit 1=datasetIndexPresent, bit 2=timeOffsetPresent, bit 3=sensorStatusPresent, bit 4=noData

characteristics.name: ASR (Air Sensor Read)
characteristics.notes: Notification characteristic. Device pushes sensor data records via this characteristic. Data format uses ASR record framing: [flags byte][sensor count or index byte][record sequence 2 bytes] [optional fields based on flags: base time, time offset, dataset index, sensor status] followed by packed sensor value bytes. Flags indicate which optional fields are present.

report_measurements.description: Request stored measurement records from a sensor dataset.

trigger_sensor_read.description: Force an immediate sensor reading (vendor command 0x07).

ui_command.description: Send UI command to device (vendor command 0x62).

command.description: 1=welcome tune, 2=low battery tune, 3=paired tune, 4=radon alert, 5=red ring breathe, 6=green ring breathe, 7=blue ring breathe, 8=measure ref waveform, 9=yellow ring breathe, 10=white breathe, 11=test RGB LEDs, 12=play selected sound, 13=exercise predefined pattern, 14=exercise with RGB components, 15=spin blue to solid

characteristics.name: ASRACP (Air Sensor Read Access Control Point)
characteristics.notes: Control point for the ASR service. Used to request historical data, configure device, set time, trigger readings, etc. Opcodes (write): 1=report measurements, 2=delete measurements, 3=abort operation, 4=count measurements, 248=vendor setup, 249=vendor readback. Indications: 1=report IA, 2=delete IA, 3=status IB, 4=count IC, 248=vendor status IB, 249=vendor status IW.

format.name: unknown
format.notes: 00 00 00 20 00 00 in capture; meaning unknown.

format.name: base_time
format.notes: Unix seconds, little-endian. Matches dataset-info base_time (device epoch — capture value was ~23 h old, agreeing with the self-check uptime, i.e. time of boot/reset).

format.name: unknown2
format.notes: 0x00 in capture.

format.name: dataset_number
format.notes: Echoes the requested dataset (0x02 in capture, matching dataset info).

format.name: radon_24h_centi
format.notes: MEDIUM confidence. Capture value 2639 = 26.39, consistent with the 26 Bq/m³ 24 h average as a 0.01-scaled value; the same u16 appears at bytes 26-27 of the self-check response.

format.name: radon_pending_hour_centi
format.notes: MEDIUM confidence. Capture value 3055 = 30.55, read as the in-progress hour's radon at 0.01 Bq/m³ — plausible but uncorroborated by a second source.

format.name: record_count
format.notes: Little-endian. Capture: 23, one less than the dataset-info record_count (24) read seconds earlier — likely counts completed hourly records excluding the pending one.

characteristics.name: ASR (Air Sensor Read)
characteristics.notes: On Griffin firmware (capture: G-BLE-2.2.3) a report-measurements write on ASRACP (see griffin_report_measurements) is answered by a SINGLE 230-byte notification on this characteristic carrying the pending hour as twelve 5-minute slots per sensor, oldest first (slot 11 matched the combined-characteristic reading taken seconds later). Requires a large ATT MTU — the vendor app negotiated 247; behavior at the default MTU 23 is unobserved. Slot arrays for sensors the model lacks are all-0xFF (Wave 2: the 144-byte region at offset 56, sized for six more 12-slot u16 arrays — presumably pressure/CO₂/VOC and friends on Wave Plus, unobserved). Layout below decoded from the long capture and cross-checked against the same session's combined-data reads (radon 26/18 Bq/m³, 22.6 °C, 53.5 %RH, light 16 all agree). This does NOT follow the legacy per-record ASR framing documented on the Wave Gen 1 ASR characteristic; that framing remains unobserved on this firmware.

characteristics.name: ASRACP (Air Sensor Read Access Control Point)
characteristics.notes: Same ASRACP protocol as Wave Gen 1, multiplexed with the newer "Griffin" direct command set on firmware G-BLE >= 1.2.1 (commands below; older firmware wraps the same operations in the 0x71 passthrough envelope). Capture-verified on G-BLE-2.2.3: writes of 0x6D/0x74/0x02/0x66/0x72 each answered by an indication echoing the opcode with a status byte (0x00 = OK). History readout (long capture): a 9-byte 0x01 report-measurements request sent as ATT Write Command (0x52, no response) triggers one 230-byte block on the ASR characteristic, then an indication here: [0x01, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00] — opcode echo, status 0x00, then likely a u16le count of blocks sent (0x0001) and a trailing u16 0x0000. See griffin_report_measurements.

format.name: reserved
format.notes: Not parsed by the app; 0x01 in capture.

format.name: ambient_light
format.notes: Raw ambient light level (0-255).

format.name: orientation_wavecount

format.name: reserved2
format.notes: Not parsed by the app; 01 00 ff ff in the setup capture, 00 00 ff ff throughout the steady-state long capture — byte 16 varies (meaning unknown), bytes 18-19 always 0xFFFF.

characteristics.name: Combined Sensor Data
characteristics.notes: Packed 20-byte multi-sensor current readings (format below). Layout from the app's CurrentValuesParser (shared with Wave Plus) and validated byte-for-byte against the capture: humidity 53.5 %, radon 13/11 Bq/m³, 24.16 °C, pressure/CO₂/VOC null (0xFF) on Wave 2, which lacks those sensors. 0xFF (uint8) or 0xFFFF (uint16, either byte 0xFF) marks an absent sensor value.

characteristics.notes: Same ASRACP protocol as Wave Gen 1.

format.name: orientation_wavecount
format.notes: Upper nibble = orientation, lower nibble = wave (gesture) count.

format.name: reserved2
format.notes: Not parsed by the app.

characteristics.name: Combined Sensor Data
characteristics.notes: Same packed 20-byte layout as the Wave Gen 2 combined characteristic (see b42e4dcc) — the app parses both with the same CurrentValuesParser, with pressure/CO₂/VOC populated here. APK-derived; the capture only exercised the Wave 2 instance. The format block below restates that shared layout so the fields are machine-readable on this characteristic too — consumers resolve a characteristic's byte layout by UUID, and a prose-only cross-reference left every Wave Plus reading undecodable. Field-level confidence matches the source: layout HIGH from the shared parser, Wave Plus values themselves not exercised in capture. 0xFF (uint8) or 0xFFFF (uint16) marks an absent sensor value.

format.name: ambient_light
format.notes: Raw ambient light level; airthings-ble runs it through its illuminance converter. Offset 0 is deliberate: of the two leading uint8s in "<2B5HLL", _decode_wave_mini reads val[0] (the FIRST byte) as illuminance; byte 1 (the second uint8) is read by neither vendor decoder. Note this differs from the Wave/Wave Plus combined packet, where byte 0 is reserved and ambient light sits at byte 2.

format.name: temperature
format.notes: Centikelvin on the wire: °C = raw/100 - 273.15 (wavemini-reader).

format.name: pressure
format.notes: raw/50 hPa per airthings-ble; wavemini-reader ignores this field.

format.name: voc
format.notes: wavemini-reader's docstring says ppm, but the Airthings app, airthings-ble/Home Assistant, and this family's own UI thresholds (griffin_ui_settings: VOC yellow/red 250/2000) all treat the raw count as ppb.

characteristics.name: Combined Sensor Data
characteristics.notes: Packed multi-sensor current readings, struct "<2B5HLL": unused, temperature, pressure, humidity, VOC, unused x3 — the packet carries pressure and VOC in addition to temperature/humidity. Confirmed by Airthings/wavemini-reader (CURR_VAL_UUID) and Airthings/airthings-ble (CHAR_UUID_WAVEMINI_DATA). Field offsets and transforms below are taken from those two readers' decode functions (wavemini-reader CurrentValues.from_bytes: temperature = u16@2/100 - 273.15, humidity = u16@6/100, voc = u16@8; airthings-ble _decode_wave_mini adds pressure = u16@4/50 and ambient light from byte 0). MEDIUM confidence: vendor-published source code, not verified against live traffic here. NOTE the temperature is centikelvin — unlike every other model in this family, which reports centidegrees Celsius.

characteristics.name: ASRACP (Air Sensor Read Access Control Point)
characteristics.notes: Access control point. Confirmed by Airthings/airthings-ble (COMMAND_UUID_WAVE_MINI) and ESPHome (ACCESS_CONTROL_POINT_CHARACTERISTIC_UUID).

services.name: View Plus Air Sensor Service
services.notes: Sibling service: b42e77de-ade7-11e4-89d3-123b93f75cba is the Airthings Hub/Bridge device's primary service UUID. View Plus's own ASR/ASRACP characteristic UUIDs were not extracted from the app; the family shares the ASR/ASRACP profile documented on the Wave and Wave Plus services above, but the View Plus UUIDs are unconfirmed and are deliberately not guessed here.

characteristics.notes: Standard BLE pressure (SIG: uint32, 0.1 Pa resolution). Available on Wave Plus. The scale below yields hPa (= mbar) directly: 0.1 Pa = 0.001 hPa. This matches the vendor app, which decodes this characteristic as uint32 LE / 1000 (DeviceDataTypes.pressureInSIFromCurrentCharacteristic).

characteristics.name: Dew Point Characteristic
characteristics.notes: Standard BLE dew point. Available on Wave Plus.

services.name: Environmental Sensing Service
services.notes: Bluetooth SIG standard Environmental Sensing Service (0x181A), the defined owner of the temperature/humidity/pressure/dew-point characteristics below. The service UUID is inferred from the SIG assignment rather than captured; the characteristic UUIDs themselves came from the vendor app.

characteristics.name: Current Time
characteristics.notes: Device RTC. Write to set device clock.

services.name: Current Time Service
services.notes: Bluetooth SIG standard Current Time Service (0x1805), the defined owner of the Current Time characteristic below. Service UUID inferred from the SIG assignment rather than captured.

characteristics.name: OAD Image Block Request
characteristics.notes: Write firmware image blocks.

characteristics.name: OAD Image Notify
characteristics.notes: Notification channel for OAD status.

characteristics.name: OAD Image Control
characteristics.notes: Control OAD transfer (start, abort, commit).

characteristics.name: OAD Image Count
characteristics.notes: Number of firmware images available.

services.name: TI OAD Firmware Update Service
services.notes: Texas Instruments Over-the-Air Download service for firmware updates. Available on most models.
